contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with and complementary to already corroborated FND-0047 (when h^0(L) jumps, do not identify the relative linear system with Proj(pi_*L) without CBC; use a divisor/Hilbert/Abel–Jacobi model instead): FND-0107 is the positive representing-object statement that FND-0047 requires, not a restatement of the obstruction alone. Compatible with FND-0046 (fibrewise O(Gamma)≅L does not automatically equal the CE Fitting scheme structure): FND-0107 models the Abel–Jacobi incidence of effective divisors with O(Gamma)≅L, not the CE evaluation Fitting ideal. Compatible with FND-0083 (RR nonemptiness of the full AJ fibre does not force reduced-support Conf_6 nonemptiness on every fibre). Primary checks. (1) Stacks 0BA0 / Lemma 44.6.7: Abel map gamma_d: Hilb^d_{X/k}->Pic^d_{X/k} exists; its scheme-theoretic fibre over [L] is Z={D: O(D)≅L}, and Z≅Proj(Sym(H^0(X,L)^*))≅P^{h^0(L)-1}; Pic_{X/k} is separated (Groupoids 047L), so graphs of sections are closed and the fibre product is closed in Hilb. (2) Stacks 0CCT: the complete linear system |D| is by definition the set of closed points of that Hilb->Pic fibre, with scheme structure P(H^0(O(D))^vee). (3) Stacks 0B9D / 056P: for smooth proper relative curves, relative effective Cartier divisors of degree d are exactly the finite locally free degree-d closed subschemes, so Hilb^d≅ relative Div^d; on smooth curves every length-d 0-cycle is Cartier, whence Hilb^d≅ Sym^d (classical Hilbert–Chow isomorphism on smooth curves; cf. Wikipedia Hilbert scheme). Relative form: same identification over any base for smooth proper C/B. (4) Stacks 02KE and Grauert/CBC: formation of pi_*L and the geometric fibres of Proj(pi_*L) agree with P(H^0(C_b,L_b)) only where h^0 is locally constant and base-change maps are isomorphisms; at jump loci rank(pi_*L) tracks the minimal h^0 and Proj fibres are strictly smaller than the true |L_b|. Over the constancy open the two models agree because zero loci of sections modulo scaling recover effective Cartier divisors. Mild scope notes (not retiral grounds): (a) relative Picard requires the usual fppf/rigidified functor (section or geometric connectedness of fibres); the fibre-product formulation already encodes that correctly; (b) mathematical scope is general smooth proper curve families, while the campaign application is the (6,6) CE degree-6 system on C66-GEO-H0; (c) do not merge into FND-0047—the equivalence groups differ (obstruction vs explicit Abel–Jacobi model) and GEO-H0 needs the representing object stated positively. Promote from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. merge_target_id: none.

scope.generality: smooth proper curve families over arbitrary bases; not special to (6,6)
scope.mathematical: For any base scheme B and any smooth proper curve family pi:C->B of relative dimension 1, and any invertible sheaf L on C of relative degree d>=0, the functor of relative effective Cartier divisors Gamma on C/B with O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to L (i.e. classifying the B-point of Pic^d_{C/B} given by L) is represented by the Abel-Jacobi fibre product Hilb^d_{C/B} x_{Pic^d_{C/B}} B, equivalently Sym^d(C/B) x_{Pic^d_{C/B}} B; this closed immersion into the relative Hilbert/symmetric product is correct over all of B. The relative projective space Proj(pi_*L) recovers the correct geometric fibres of that linear system only over the open locus of B where b |-> h^0(C_b,L_b) is locally constant and cohomology-and-base-change holds; over that open the two models agree. Applies in particular to the C66-GEO-H0 relative degree-6 linear system L=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} on the balanced tetragonal CE family for (g,n)=(6,6).
